name: Anonymous U.S. marketing-organization post-hire incident

attribution.legal_posture: Sophos-authored anonymous incident assessment; it carries no charge, adjudication, sanctions designation, civil-identity finding, or named victim report.

caveats: The record covers account-level observations; malware, theft, exfiltration, persistence beyond the account, and specific harmed-data status are unreported.
Sophos's Russia statement interprets a blocked sign-in; physical-location or residence history remain unverified.
The employer and worker are unnamed; identity resolution and victim deanonymization are outside the record.
The source supplies Sophos's assessment rather than a criminal charge, adjudication, sanctions designation, or nationality determination.

statements: Sophos reports that an unnamed remote developer remained employed for roughly six months at an approximately 1,000-employee U.S. marketing organization.
The account had highly privileged AWS access and persistently used an anomalous VPN.

Sophos says Microsoft 365 Conditional Access blocked a sign-in and led its analysts to assess that the user was located in Russia; correlated identity and cloud-access evidence prompted account disablement and an access audit.

sources.support: The Sophos-hosted timeline corroborates the anonymous marketing-sector customer profile, approximately six-month employment duration, suspicious VPN use, a blocked Microsoft 365 sign-in that Sophos interpreted as locating the user in Russia, highly privileged AWS access, and the account disablement and audit response. PDF metadata predates the public case-page date and is not treated as an independently published incident. Evidence boundary: Companion asset in the same Sophos incident-publication family. It is not independent corroboration and does not identify the worker or customer
sources.locator: Organization profile; adversary behavior; threat detection; investigation; response timeline

sources.support: Sophos reports an unnamed remote developer at an approximately 1,000-employee U.S. marketing organization who remained employed for roughly six months, had highly privileged AWS access, and persistently used an anomalous VPN. Sophos says a Microsoft 365 sign-in blocked by Conditional Access led its analysts to assess that the user was located in Russia; the provider correlated VPN, identity, and cloud-access evidence, after which the customer disabled the account and audited access. Evidence boundary: Provider-authored anonymous customer case attributed by Sophos to a DPRK-linked fake IT worker. It is not a public charge, adjudication, sanctions designation, victim identification, or proof of malware, theft, or exfiltration
sources.locator: Customer profile; proactive-hunt timeline; Microsoft 365 Conditional Access and AWS findings; customer response
